lore.mythicrelics.ancile:
In King Numa's time a figure-eight shield of Mars fell from the sky: as long as Rome kept it, Rome would not fall.\
Numa had eleven identical copies made so no one would know which to steal.
lore.mythicrelics.andvaranaut:
The ring of the dwarf Andvari, which made gold grow. When Loki stole it, Andvari cursed it: it would bring ruin to all its owners.\
So it was with Hreidmar, with Fafnir and with Sigurd.
lore.mythicrelics.ankh: The key of life. The gods are shown holding it to the pharaoh's nose to give him the breath of eternal life.
lore.mythicrelics.anubis_scepter:
The *was* scepter, topped with an animal's head and forked at the base, was carried by the gods as a symbol of power.\
In the Hall of Two Truths, Anubis weighed the heart of the dead against the feather of Ma'at: that is his judgment.
lore.mythicrelics.anubis_set: Whoever wears the mask and the ring and carries the scepter is known as a servant of Anubis: the dead will not attack them unless disturbed.
lore.mythicrelics.ariadne_thread: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread to enter the Minotaur's labyrinth and find the way out.
lore.mythicrelics.athena_aegis:
The aegis, Zeus' goatskin worn by Athena, bore the gorgoneion, Medusa's face that terrified enemies.\
Athena gave Perseus the polished shield so he wouldn't look at Medusa.
lore.mythicrelics.augur_lituus:
Augurs read the will of the gods in the flight of birds, marking out the sky with the lituus, a curved staff.\
Romulus won the right to found Rome because he saw twelve vultures and his brother only six.
lore.mythicrelics.bastet_amulet:
Bastet, the cat goddess, protected the home, mothers and children. Egyptians revered cats because they hunted snakes and rats.\
In early times Bastet was a warrior lioness, like Sekhmet.
lore.mythicrelics.brisingamen:
The necklace of the goddess Freyja, forged by four dwarves.\
Freyja was goddess of love and fertility, and received in her hall half of the warriors slain in battle.
lore.mythicrelics.cerberus_collar:
Cerberus, the three-headed hound, guarded the gate of Hades: he let the dead in and let no one out.\
Capturing him was the last of Heracles' twelve labours; he dragged him out in chains.
lore.mythicrelics.charon_obol:
Greeks placed an obol in the mouth of their dead to pay Charon the crossing to Hades. Without payment, the soul wandered the shore for a hundred years.\
Athens' obol bore Athena's owl.
lore.mythicrelics.draupnir: Odin's gold ring, forged by the same dwarves as Mjölnir. Every ninth night eight equal rings dripped from it.
lore.mythicrelics.egypt.intro:
Relics are not crafted: they are found. Egypt's rest in the chests of desert pyramids, and now and then in the houses of desert villages.\
The more powerful the relic, the harder it is to find.
lore.mythicrelics.eye_of_horus:
In their struggle for the throne, Set tore out one of Horus's eyes, and Thoth healed it.\
The wedjat, the restored eye, became the amulet of protection, healing and wholeness.
lore.mythicrelics.gjallarhorn:
The horn of Heimdall, warden of the Bifröst bridge, who sees and hears everything.\
Its blast is heard in all nine worlds and will herald Ragnarök.
lore.mythicrelics.gleipnir:
The only fetter that could hold the wolf Fenrir. The dwarves made it from six things that don't exist: the sound of a cat's footfall, a woman's beard, the roots of a mountain, a bear's sinews, a fish's breath and a bird's spittle.\
It was thin and soft as a silk ribbon.
lore.mythicrelics.golden_fleece:
The fleece of Chrysomallos, the golden winged ram, hung from an oak in Colchis, guarded by a dragon that never slept.\
Jason and the Argonauts sought it because bringing it back was the test to claim the throne: it was the sign of the rightful king.
lore.mythicrelics.golden_scarab:
Khepri, the scarab god, rolled the sun across the sky the way a dung beetle rolls its ball, and brought it back to life every morning.\
Egyptians wore scarab amulets as a symbol of rebirth and protection.
lore.mythicrelics.greece.intro:
Greece left no pyramids: its relics lie where their myths fit. Ancient ruins are brushed, the labyrinth keeps the thread, the Nether is Hades' realm and the ancient city is Orpheus' descent.\
Perseus gathered the gifts of the gods to defeat Medusa.
lore.mythicrelics.gungnir:
Odin's spear, forged by the sons of Ivaldi. It never misses its mark.\
Odin hurled it over the Vanir host to begin the first war in the world.
lore.mythicrelics.hades_helm:
The cyclopes forged for Hades a helm that makes its wearer invisible.\
Athena and Perseus also used it; with it, Perseus escaped the gorgons.
lore.mythicrelics.hermes_sandals:
Hermes, messenger of the gods, flew with his winged sandals. He also guided the souls of the dead to the underworld.\
He lent them to Perseus to go after Medusa.
lore.mythicrelics.icarus_wings:
Daedalus, architect of the labyrinth, made wings of feathers held with wax to escape Crete with his son Icarus.\
He warned him not to fly too high, for the sun melts the wax, nor too low, for the sea soaks the feathers. Icarus flew too high and fell into the sea.
lore.mythicrelics.idunn_apples:
The goddess Iðunn kept in a basket the apples that kept the gods young.\
When the giant Þjazi abducted her, the gods began to age.
lore.mythicrelics.jackal_mask: Anubis guided the souls of the dead to their judgment. Priests who embalmed the dead wore jackal masks to embody him.
lore.mythicrelics.jackal_ring: Jackals prowled the desert cemeteries. That is why the Egyptians made Anubis, the jackal-headed god, the guardian of tombs.
lore.mythicrelics.janus_key:
Janus, the two-faced god, kept doors, beginnings and passages: one face looks back, the other ahead.\
He was shown holding a key; his temple's doors opened in war and closed in peace.
lore.mythicrelics.jarngreipr: Thor's iron gloves. He needed them to wield Mjölnir, which glowed red-hot when it came back.
lore.mythicrelics.medusa_head:
Medusa, the gorgon, turned to stone whoever looked at her.\
Perseus beheaded her looking at her reflection in Athena's shield, and used her head as a weapon.
lore.mythicrelics.megingjord: Thor's belt of strength: when he girded it, his divine strength doubled.
lore.mythicrelics.mimir_head:
Mímir was the wisest of the gods. When the Vanir beheaded him, Odin smeared his head with herbs so it would not rot and chanted charms over it.\
So the head spoke and told Odin what no one else knew.
lore.mythicrelics.mjolnir:
Thor's hammer was forged by the dwarves Brokkr and Sindri. Loki, as a gadfly, stung Brokkr's eyelid, and so the handle came out short.\
Mjölnir never misses and always returns to Thor's hand.
lore.mythicrelics.mummy_wraps:
Embalmers wrapped the body in hundreds of meters of linen to preserve it for the afterlife.\
The husks of the desert recognize those wraps as their own.
lore.mythicrelics.norse.intro:
Almost every treasure of the Norse gods was forged by the dwarves: Thor's hammer, Odin's spear and ring, and the ribbon that bound Fenrir.\
They lie where their myths fit: the cold north, the dwarves' mines and the trials of heroes.
lore.mythicrelics.odin_ravens: Odin's ravens, Thought and Memory. Every morning they fly over the whole world and, when they return, whisper to him all they have seen.
lore.mythicrelics.odrerir:
The mead of poetry, brewed from the blood of wise Kvasir: whoever drank it became a poet or a scholar.\
Odin stole it from the giants in the shape of an eagle.
lore.mythicrelics.orpheus_lyre:
Orpheus' music enchanted animals, trees and stones.\
He went down to the underworld for Eurydice and with his lyre moved Hades and lulled its guardians to sleep.
lore.mythicrelics.osiris_crook:
Osiris, king of Egypt, was murdered by his brother Set and brought back to life by Isis. He became lord of the afterlife and god of farming and of the Nile flood.\
The crook, the shepherd's guide, is one of the pharaoh's insignia.
lore.mythicrelics.osiris_flail:
The flail is the pharaoh's other insignia. Its origin is debated: a threshing tool, a shepherd's fly whisk or a tool for gathering resin.\
Together with the crook, it stands for the power and abundance Osiris brought with the Nile.
lore.mythicrelics.osiris_set: Osiris is the god who died and came back to life. Whoever bears both of his insignia shares a little of that rebirth.
lore.mythicrelics.palladium:
A wooden statuette of Pallas that protected Troy: the city could not fall while it was kept.\
Aeneas brought it to Italy, and the Romans guarded it in the temple of Vesta.
lore.mythicrelics.pandora_jar:
Zeus gave Pandora, the first woman, a jar she must not open. When she opened it, every evil escaped into the world; only Hope remained inside.\
It was a pithos, a jar: the "box" comes from a mistranslation.
lore.mythicrelics.perseus_set: With Hermes' sandals, Hades' helm and Athena's shield, Perseus could approach Medusa unseen, without looking at her, and fly away.
lore.mythicrelics.prometheus_fennel:
The titan Prometheus stole fire from the gods, hiding an ember in a hollow fennel stalk, and gave it to humankind along with the arts.\
Zeus chained him to a rock, where an eagle ate his liver every day.
lore.mythicrelics.ra_disk:
Ra, the sun god, crosses the sky in his barque by day and by night travels through the Duat, the underworld, where he battles Apep, the serpent of chaos.\
On his head he wears the sun disk encircled by the uraeus, the cobra that spits fire at his enemies.
lore.mythicrelics.rome.intro:
Rome's great gods are the Greek ones under other names, so these relics come from what is Rome's own: guarding the city and the hearth, and reading the will of the gods.\
Rome left no structures in the world: each relic lies where its myth fits.
lore.mythicrelics.sekhmet_claws:
Sekhmet, the lioness of war, “the Powerful One”. Ra sent her to punish humanity and she fell into a blood frenzy; she was only stopped when the fields were flooded with beer dyed red, which she drank believing it was blood.\
She was also a goddess of healing, and her breath was said to be the hot desert wind.
lore.mythicrelics.sibylline_books:
The Sibyl of Cumae offered King Tarquin nine books of prophecy. When he refused to pay, she burned three, then three more; the king ended up paying the full price for the last three.\
Rome consulted them in times of crisis.
lore.mythicrelics.skidbladnir: The ship of the god Freyr, made by the sons of Ivaldi. It held all the gods with their weapons, always had a fair wind and folded like a cloth to be carried in a pocket.
lore.mythicrelics.sleipnir_horseshoe:
Sleipnir, Odin's eight-legged horse, was the fastest of all. He galloped through the air and over the sea.\
Hermóðr rode him down to Hel to plead for Baldr.
lore.mythicrelics.styx_water:
Thetis dipped her son Achilles in the river Styx to make him invulnerable. She held him by the heel, which stayed dry.\
At Troy, Paris killed him with an arrow to the heel.
lore.mythicrelics.thor_set: Thor could not wield Mjölnir without his iron gloves, and with the belt of strength his might doubled: together, the three are the god of thunder.
lore.mythicrelics.thoth_palette:
Thoth, the ibis god of writing, wisdom and the moon, was the scribe of the gods: he invented hieroglyphs and records the weighing of the heart at the judgment of the dead.\
Scribes wrote with reed pens and red and black ink, kept in their palette.
lore.mythicrelics.vesta_lamp:
Vesta was the goddess of the hearth. Her sacred fire burned forever in her temple, tended by the Vestals.\
If it went out, it was a terrible omen for Rome.
lore.mythicrelics.wolf_bulla:
A she-wolf nursed Romulus and Remus by the Tiber, which is why the wolf is Rome's emblem.\
Roman children wore a bulla around the neck, a locket against evil, until they came of age.
